title: Biobank of Cardiomyopathies Ulm
summary:
Cardiomyopathies are common cardiac diseases often leading to increased mortality and reduced quality of life. Genetic factors as well as environmental influences play an essential role in pathogenesis of cardiomyopathies. However, detailed genetic and molecular underpinnings of this severe cardiac disorder are not fully understood yet.
Biobanking of biomaterials such as blood, urine and myocardial tissue has emerged as a powerful tool in modern biomedical science to combine patient-specific data and individual genetic background. 
Since it has been shown in recent years that diseases of the heart muscle, such as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, are genetically predisposed, phenotype data and biomaterials collected from affected patients should be used to uncover disease-related genetic mechanisms of certain forms of cardiomyopathy.
With the help of biomaterials from patients suffering from cardiomyopathies it can be also examined whether and how further pathomechniasms such as immune-mediated processes are involved in the formation and expression of certain forms of cardiomyopathy. Further biomaterial-based analyzis should be used to estimate the success of established clincal therapy.

interventions.name:
Propspective observational study to collect baseline characteristics, outcome data as well as biomaterial samples to evaluate diagnostic and therapeutic strategies of patients suffering from cardiomyopathies.
Date of study visits correspond with the routinely dates of clinical follow-up.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
acquired and/or inherited cardiomyopathy
Exclusion criteria:
Cardiomyopathy caused  by:

- arterial hypertension
- ischemic cardiomyopathy
- toxic cardiomyopathy
- aortic stenosis
